If there’s one thing I don’t like about more modern anime, it’s the abandonment of overt philosophical thinking. Cowboy Bebop explored concepts of Zen Buddhism, Trigun explored pacifism, Death Note explored moral relativism, etc. There always seemed to be some core concept that the anime was built on. Now don’t get me wrong there is still a lot of this out there. Vinland Saga had a very deep exploration in the meaning of what it is to be a real warrior. However, a conversation and a video shown to me yesterday made me think about Ghost in the Shell for the first time in a while.

At its core, it is the concept of what it means to be human. The argument about the ship being replaced 1 part at a time comes to mind. At what point is it no longer the same ship? The characters mostly have cybernetic bodies, but all of them were born human. The Ghost is that intangible part of us that recognizes existence. The whole is greater than the sum of its parts. The AI in the story responds to a monologue by The Major about this with a quote about seeing the world as dim images in a mirror. Just as we are not all that we see, so is the world. It was in fact a quote from Paul in the Bible. However this concept is reflected in other faiths as well. There is more to this world than that which we see and measure.
